title: Salting, peppering and key derivation (bcrypt, Argon2)

videos.script: A password store will leak one day. Plan for that day. {{title}} The question is what the thief gets. With a plain hash, they get a lot. Three of Vereda's staff chose the same password, and the store shows it at a glance. {{audit}} Worse, that hash is the same in every database in the world. {{same}} A salt fixes both. Each account gets its own random value, mixed in before hashing. {{salt}} But a fast hash, salted or not, still lets an attacker try billions of guesses a second. So password storage uses functions built to be slow. bcrypt, and now Argon2id. {{slow}} Then two refinements. A pepper, a secret kept outside the database. {{pepper}} And a way to raise the cost later, without asking anybody to change their password. {{upgrade}}
